Context

A contributor can build SpaceApp, run its test suites and run a simulated CLI task (`npm run smoke:offline`), but cannot easily run the **whole application from source**. `CONTRIBUTING.md` has no instructions for it. The root scripts `dev:api`, `dev:web` and `dev:worker` each start one process and expect everything else to be there already. In an installed SpaceApp, the containers wire that up (`deploy/docker/*-entrypoint.sh`, `core-supervisor.mjs`, `packages/run-spaceapp/templates/compose.yml`):

- PostgreSQL with pgvector, and the migrations;
- Temporal for the worker;
- the CLI host on a Unix socket, with the `*-vscode-parity` wrapper commands it launches;
- a session secret, the one-time owner setup token, and a few dozen `SPACE_*` paths.

So anyone who wants to change a pane, the Room Agent or the memory graph and see the result in a browser must rebuild Docker images, or reverse-engineer the entrypoints. [`KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md`](https://github.com/oll4com/spaceapp/blob/main/docs/quality/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md) lists this as ONB-001: "Configuration surface and contributor setup complex".

## Goal

After `npm ci` on a fresh clone, one command starts a working SpaceApp from source with hot reload, on Linux, macOS and Windows 11 (WSL2). One command stops it, and one removes everything it created.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm run dev:stack` starts, in order:
  - PostgreSQL (pgvector) and Temporal in Docker;
  - the migrations;
  - the API (watch mode), the Vite web dev server, the Temporal worker, and the CLI host (`packages/cli-host`) from source.

  It then prints the URL and a one-time owner setup token. `npm run dev:stack -- down` stops everything. `npm run dev:stack -- reset` removes only the containers, volumes and state directory this command created.
- [ ] The Docker services use the same images, pinned by digest, as `packages/run-spaceapp/templates/compose.yml`. The digests are read from that file or from one shared place, never copied by hand.
- [ ] Isolation from an installed SpaceApp: its own compose project name, its own state directory (for example `.dev-stack/`, git-ignored), and ports that do not collide with an install on 4910/4911. Ports can be changed through environment variables. Every port it opens binds to `127.0.0.1` only, including Vite, PostgreSQL and Temporal.
- [ ] Secrets (database password, session secret, setup token) are generated per state directory with mode 0600. They are never printed, apart from the setup token, and never committed. The usual owner setup works: setup token → create owner → sign in. The dev-login shortcut is not used.
- [ ] Hot reload: a change in `apps/api/src` restarts the API, a change in `apps/web/src` hot-reloads in the browser, and a change in `packages/*` is rebuilt and picked up (or a single documented command does it).
- [ ] CLI panes: the Getting Started room opens, and an OpenCode pane starts through the from-source CLI host and shows OpenCode's terminal UI. The pinned `opencode-ai` version from the `Dockerfile` is installed into the state directory, not globally. Wrapper commands and provider state also live in the state directory. No AI provider account is needed to reach the OpenCode UI.
- [ ] `/readyz` reports `ok: true` with workflows enabled. Stopping one process (for example the worker) shows up as a clear failure in the dev-stack output, not a silent hang.
- [ ] CI: a job on `ubuntu-latest` runs `dev:stack` without a TTY, waits for `/readyz`, completes owner setup over HTTP, opens a CLI pane through the API, checks that the pane is running, then runs `reset` and checks that no container, volume or process is left.
- [ ] Docs: a "Run the full app from source" section in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (prerequisites, commands, ports, troubleshooting), plus the platform notes for macOS (Docker Desktop or Colima) and Windows 11 (WSL2). The PR contains the terminal output of a run on Linux and on at least one of macOS or WSL2.

## How to test

```sh
git clone https://github.com/oll4com/spaceapp && cd spaceapp
ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1 npm ci
npm run dev:stack            # open the printed URL, create the owner, open Getting Started, start an OpenCode pane
# edit apps/web/src/... and apps/api/src/... and watch the reloads
npm run dev:stack -- down
npm run dev:stack -- reset   # docker ps -a / docker volume ls show nothing left from it
```

## Out of scope

- The browser service (`packages/browser-host`, Chromium) and the optional companion services. They may stay disabled in the dev stack, with a clear message in the UI as today.
- Root-only features (admin shell, host-root access).
- Changing how the published images or the `run-spaceapp` launcher work.
- Running the CLIs of providers other than OpenCode (they can be added later through the same wrapper mechanism).

## Pointers

- `deploy/docker/core-entrypoint.sh`, `deploy/docker/core-supervisor.mjs`, `deploy/docker/cli-entrypoint.sh`, `deploy/docker/public-cli-wrapper.sh` (what the containers set up today)
- `packages/run-spaceapp/templates/compose.yml` (environment of every service, pinned images)
- `apps/api/src/config.ts`, `apps/api/src/config-registry.ts` and `npm run config:reference -w @space/api` (every API setting and its default), `docs/configuration-reference.md`
- `packages/cli-host/src/main.ts` (`SPACE_CLI_HOST_SOCKET` and other host settings), `scripts/contributor-smoke.mjs` (how the offline smoke drives the CLI host)
- `apps/web/vite.config.ts` (dev proxy to the API on 4910), `packages/db` (`npm run db:migrate`)
- Before opening a PR, run the checks in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/oll4com/spaceapp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks-before-a-commit).

That stage copies the **whole** monorepo output into every image: all of `node_modules` after `npm prune --omit=dev`, all of `apps/`, all of `packages/` and `agent-skills/`. So:

- the CLI image ships the API, the web app, the Temporal SDK with its native core bridge, pdfjs and `@napi-rs/canvas`, though it only runs `packages/cli-host/dist/main.js`;
- the browser image ships the CLI host, `node-pty`, the web app and the Temporal SDK, though it only runs `apps/api/dist/browser-host-main.js`;
- the core image ships the CLI host and `node-pty`, plus native prebuilds for platforms it never runs on.

Sizes in the latest Container matrix run on `main` (`scripts/container-image-size-budget.mjs`):

| Image | linux/amd64 | linux/arm64 | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| core | 1044.7 MiB | 1066.9 MiB | 1100 MiB |
| browser | 1719.9 MiB | 1735.0 MiB | 1750 MiB |
| cli | 1386.0 MiB | 1237.1 MiB | 2800 MiB |

The browser image is 15 MiB from its budget. The core budget already had to be raised for 1.1.5, and [`KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md`](https://github.com/oll4com/spaceapp/blob/main/docs/quality/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md) (EXT-C-F20) names the core image size as the reason some functionality cannot be added to core. Every user downloads these images on install and on every `update`.

## Goal

Each image contains only what its service runs, on both architectures, with no change in behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each target gets its own production dependency closure, for example a per-target build stage that installs only the workspaces that target runs, or a pruned deploy directory per entrypoint. Shared layers stay shared where it helps the total download.
- [ ] Measured with `scripts/container-image-size-budget.mjs` on **both** `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`:
  - core at most 850 MiB,
  - browser at most 1350 MiB,
  - cli at most 1000 MiB.

  The budgets in the script and its test (`scripts/tests/container-image-size-budget.test.mjs`) are lowered to the new sizes plus a small margin, with the measurements recorded in the comment as today.
- [ ] No functional change. Each image keeps its entrypoint, the non-root `spaceapp` user (uid/gid 10001), the healthcheck, `/app/deploy/docker/*` scripts, the `*-vscode-parity` wrapper links, OpenCode in the CLI image, `LICENSE`/`NOTICE`/`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, the owner and backup scripts in core, and the security patches applied to npm in `runtime-base`.
- [ ] Smoke checks in `.github/workflows/containers.yml` for every target and architecture, so a missing module fails CI instead of an install:
  - core starts against a pgvector PostgreSQL service, runs migrations and answers `/readyz` with `ok: true`;
  - cli starts the CLI host and accepts a connection on its socket;
  - browser starts the Browser Host and launches headless Chromium once.
- [ ] Full-stack check with the launcher on Linux: build the three images locally, tag them as the version the launcher expects, run `install --profile large`, and confirm that an OpenCode pane starts and a browser pane opens a page. Put the steps and output in the PR.
- [ ] The security workflow's image scans (`.github/workflows/security.yml`) and the release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) still pass. `scripts/tests/public-docker-distribution.test.mjs` and `scripts/tests/public-compose-config.test.mjs` are updated where they assert the Dockerfile layout.
- [ ] The README's disk requirements are updated if the smaller images change them.

## How to test

```sh
for target in core browser cli; do
  docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --target "$target" -t "spaceapp-local:$target-amd64" --load .
  node scripts/container-image-size-budget.mjs --target "$target" --image "spaceapp-local:$target-amd64"
done
# repeat with --platform linux/arm64 (QEMU), as .github/workflows/containers.yml does
node --test scripts/tests/*.test.mjs
```

Then run the smoke checks above and a launcher install against the local images.

## Out of scope

- Changing the base image (Debian trixie slim with Node 22), the Node version or the Chromium source.
- Moving features between services, for example moving OpenCode into core (EXT-C-F20 describes that trade-off).

Context

The `run-spaceapp` launcher (`packages/run-spaceapp`) installs and runs SpaceApp as a Docker Compose stack (`templates/compose.yml`: core, CLI, browser, PostgreSQL/pgvector, Temporal). Docker is the only supported engine. The launcher detects Docker and installs it if missing, and every lifecycle command (`install`, `up`, `down`, `status`, `logs`, `update`, `rollback`, `backup`, `restore`, `doctor`, `repair`, `uninstall`, `factory-reset`, `provider install`, `credentials set`, `owner …`) runs `docker compose …` or `docker …` (`composeCommand` in `src/index.mjs`, `spawnTrustedCommand` in `src/cli.mjs`, probes in `src/prerequisites.mjs` and `src/storage.mjs`).

Many developers cannot or will not run a root Docker daemon: Fedora, RHEL and openSUSE ship Podman, some companies do not license Docker Desktop, and rootless containers are the safer default on a shared workstation. Today these users cannot install SpaceApp at all.

## Goal

`run-spaceapp` runs the full stack on **rootless Podman** on Linux, and on **Podman machine** on macOS, with the same commands and the same data safety as on Docker. Docker stays the default, and nothing changes for Docker users.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Engine selection: `--engine docker|podman` on `install`, saved in the launcher configuration and used by every later command. `install` without `--engine` keeps using Docker when it works. If only Podman is present it offers Podman (or picks it with `--non-interactive`) instead of installing Docker. The choice also works through `--answers`.
- [ ] Compose: the launcher uses `podman compose` (state the supported compose provider and minimum versions, for example Podman ≥ 5 with docker-compose v2 as provider) and keeps all features the template uses: profiles, file-based secrets, `depends_on` health conditions (including `required: false`), `init`, `mem_limit`/`cpus`, named volumes shared between services for the Unix sockets, `--wait`, and `exec`/`run` with `--user 10001:10001`.
- [ ] Linux rootless (Podman ≥ 5, cgroup v2): `install`, `up`, `status`, `logs`, `down`, `update` (with its checkpoint), `rollback`, `backup`, `restore`, `doctor`, `doctor --fix`, `provider install opencode`, `uninstall` and `uninstall --purge-data` all work for the `small`, `medium` and `large` profiles. The web app answers on `http://127.0.0.1:4911` and `/readyz` reports ok.
- [ ] Bind mounts registered with `workspace add` (read-write and `--read-only`) work on a host with SELinux enforcing (for example Fedora), and agents can read and write files there with correct ownership on the host.
- [ ] macOS: `install --engine podman --profile small` works on a Podman machine. The launcher checks that the machine has enough CPU, memory and disk for the profile and explains how to resize it if not.
- [ ] `doctor` reports the engine, version, rootless or rootful, the cgroup version and whether CPU/memory limits are delegated. If a limit cannot be applied it says so clearly instead of failing late. `support-bundle` includes the same facts, without secrets.
- [ ] Data safety: switching engines on an existing installation is refused with a clear message (Docker volumes are not visible to Podman), unless an explicit, documented migration path through `backup`/`restore` is implemented and tested.
- [ ] `--access host-root` is refused on Podman with a clear message. It may be supported instead, but only with tests.
- [ ] Unit tests in `packages/run-spaceapp/tests` cover command construction and engine detection for both engines. The existing tests pass unchanged for Docker.
- [ ] CI: a job on `ubuntu-latest` (it ships Podman) installs the `small` profile with `--engine podman --non-interactive`, waits for `/readyz`, runs `backup`, then `uninstall --purge-data`, and leaves nothing running.
- [ ] Docs: the launcher README, the main README prerequisites and `docs/getting-started.md` describe Podman support and its limits.

## How to test

```sh
ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1 npm ci
npm test -w run-spaceapp
npm run check -w run-spaceapp
# On a Linux host with rootless Podman (for example a Fedora VM):
node packages/run-spaceapp/bin/spaceapp.mjs install --engine podman --profile small
node packages/run-spaceapp/bin/spaceapp.mjs doctor
node packages/run-spaceapp/bin/spaceapp.mjs backup
node packages/run-spaceapp/bin/spaceapp.mjs uninstall --purge-data
```

Repeat with `--profile large` (browser service included), and on macOS with `podman machine`. Put the terminal output of each run in the PR.

## Out of scope

- Windows (Podman Desktop on WSL).
- Installing Podman itself. The launcher may print install instructions per distribution.
- Kubernetes manifests, Quadlet/systemd units, or Podman-specific images (the published images must stay the same).
- Other engines (nerdctl, Colima's containerd mode).

Context

The Memory workspace has a 3D view of the memory graph (files, memory records, topics and their relations). It is one of SpaceApp's most visible features. Today it does not scale:

- **Rendering** (`apps/web/src/features/memory-workspace/MemoryGraph3D.tsx`) uses Canvas 2D. Every frame it projects every node on the CPU, sorts all nodes by depth, strokes every edge as its own path and draws every node with `arc()`. Hover and click hit-testing is a linear scan.
- **Layout** (`layoutMemoryNetwork3D` in `memory-3d.ts`, run in `memory-network-layout.worker.ts`) is a fixed 180-step force simulation with a hash-map spatial grid that is rebuilt each step. It finishes before anything is drawn.
- **Data**: the overview endpoint (`GET /api/admin/memory/graph/overview` in `apps/api/src/memory-graph-routes.ts`) returns at most 2,000 nodes (`selectOverviewNodes`) and 6,000 edges. It sets `truncated: true` beyond that, so larger memories are only ever shown as a sample.

Long-running workspaces easily pass 2,000 nodes, and they are the users who get the most out of the memory graph.

## Goal

The 3D view renders and interacts smoothly with **50,000 nodes and 150,000 edges**, and lets the user load the full graph instead of a 2,000-node sample.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A WebGL2 renderer replaces the Canvas 2D drawing in the 3D view: instanced nodes, batched edges, depth handled by the GPU (no per-frame CPU sort of all nodes), and colors, sizes and focus/neighbor highlighting matching the current look.
- [ ] Picking (hover and click) takes at most 4 ms at 50k nodes, using GPU picking or a spatial index (no linear scan per pointer move).
- [ ] Labels: the current rules stay (core and source labels first, collision avoidance, the `showTitles` toggle), now with level-of-detail. At most a bounded number of labels are measured and drawn per frame, whatever the graph size.
- [ ] Layout runs in the existing Web Worker, incrementally: positions stream to the main thread while the simulation converges, and the view can be used during layout. No main-thread long task over 100 ms during load or layout at 50k nodes. The output is deterministic for the same input, as it is today (`apps/web/tests/memory-3d.test.ts`).
- [ ] Data: the 3D view can request more than 2,000 nodes. One option is a `limit` parameter on the overview endpoint with a hard server maximum (at least 50,000) and the default left unchanged. Another is a paged or compact endpoint. Labels keep going through the existing redaction (`redactedNode`). The route stays admin-only. Response size and server time at 50k nodes are measured and reported in the PR.
- [ ] Performance at 50k nodes / 150k edges on a laptop with an integrated GPU (state the hardware in the PR): p95 frame time at most 33 ms while rotating and zooming. At the current 2,000-node size: p95 at most 16.7 ms. Attach the measurement (a Chrome performance trace or a small frame-time harness).
- [ ] Fallback: without WebGL2, or after a context loss, the view falls back to the current Canvas 2D renderer (with the current 2,000-node cap) and keeps working. A lost context is restored when the browser allows it.
- [ ] Accessibility stays as it is: keyboard rotation and zoom, focusable canvas, `aria-label`, `aria-busy` while loading, and the existing `data-*` attributes tests rely on (`data-rotation`, `data-layout-volume`, `data-titles-visible`).
- [ ] Demo mode (`/demo-workspace`, `apps/web/src/demo/DemoStore.ts`) can generate a synthetic graph of a given size, so anyone can reproduce the benchmark without a backend or embeddings provider.
- [ ] Unit tests for the pure parts (camera/projection math, picking, label LOD selection, layout streaming) and API tests for the new limit or endpoint (`apps/api/tests/memory-graph-api.test.ts`). Existing web and API tests pass.
- [ ] No new rendering dependency (three.js, regl, deck.gl, ...) unless it is proposed and agreed in this issue first. WebGL2 is enough for points and lines.

## How to test

```sh
ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1 npm ci
npm run check
npm test -w @space/web -- memory
npm test -w @space/api -- memory-graph
npm run dev:web     # then open http://127.0.0.1:4911/demo-workspace, open Memory, switch to 3D
```

Use the synthetic demo graph at 2k, 10k and 50k nodes. Rotate, zoom, hover and click nodes, toggle titles, and record frame times. Repeat with WebGL disabled (`chrome://flags` or `--disable-webgl`) to check the fallback.

## Out of scope

- The 2D map (`DesktopMemoryGraph.tsx`, sigma.js).
- Changes to how memory is indexed, embedded or stored, or to the graph's node and edge types.
- VR/XR, screenshots or export of the graph.

## Pointers

- `apps/web/src/features/memory-workspace/MemoryGraph3D.tsx` (renderer, camera input, hit testing)
- `apps/web/src/features/memory-workspace/memory-3d.ts` (`layoutMemoryNetwork3D`, `projectMemoryPoint`, camera), `memory-network-layout.worker.ts`, `memory-network-layout.ts`
- `apps/web/src/features/memory-workspace/MemoryWorkspace.tsx`, `memory-graph-visuals.ts`, `memory-atlas.ts`
- `apps/api/src/memory-graph-routes.ts` (`selectOverviewNodes`, the overview route), `packages/contracts/src/schemas.ts` (`listMemoryGraphOverviewQuerySchema`, `memoryGraphOverviewPayloadSchema`)
- Tests: `apps/web/tests/memory-3d.test.ts`, `apps/web/tests/memory-workspace.test.tsx`, `apps/api/tests/memory-graph-api.test.ts`

Context

The API can already export its request spans over OTLP/HTTP JSON. The exporter has no dependencies, is off by default and is switched on with `SPACE_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (`apps/api/src/otlp-span-exporter.ts`). When the API starts a Temporal workflow it passes a W3C `traceparent` in the workflow input and in the Temporal memo (`apps/api/src/turns.ts`, `workflowCorrelationMemo` in `apps/api/src/trace-context.ts`). The worker reads it for its structured activity logs (`apps/worker/src/activity-observability.ts`).

But the trace stops at the API. Workers emit no spans, so a slow or failing Room Agent mission, chat turn or memory repair can only be followed by joining log lines by hand. [`docs/quality/observability.md`](https://github.com/oll4com/spaceapp/blob/main/docs/quality/observability.md#not-covered) lists this under "Not covered": "Span export covers API requests only" and "Background continuations start a new trace". In [`KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md`](https://github.com/oll4com/spaceapp/blob/main/docs/quality/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md) this is OBS-001 / OBS-007: "worker/host spans" are still open.

## Goal

With `SPACE_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` set, one API request that starts work on Temporal produces **one connected trace**: the API SERVER span, then the workflow execution, then every activity attempt. The trace shows in any OTLP backend (Jaeger, Tempo, Honeycomb, ...) without extra glue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every Temporal worker process in `apps/worker` (`worker.ts`, `memory-maintenance-worker.ts`, `memory-mutation-worker.ts`) exports spans to `<endpoint>/v1/traces` when `SPACE_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set, and does nothing when it is not.
- [ ] The exporter has the same guarantees as the API exporter: a bounded queue that drops spans and counts the drops, a timeout on each POST, and a slow or failing collector never delays or fails workflow or activity work. The code is shared with the API, not copied. For example, move it into a workspace package and keep the API behavior and its tests (`apps/api/tests/otlp-span-exporter.test.ts`) unchanged.
- [ ] Span tree for a workflow started by the API (`codexAppServerTurnWorkflow`, `roomAgentSupervisorWorkflow` missions, `roomAgentActionWorkflow`, `dotGoalWorkflow`, memory workflows):
  - a workflow span whose parent is the span id from the propagated `traceparent`;
  - one span per activity attempt, child of the workflow span, with the attempt number, outcome and the existing `reasonCode` / `category`;
  - child workflows (`memoryMaintenanceWorkflow` → `memoryConsolidationWorkflow`) nest under their parent.
- [ ] Determinism: workflow code does no I/O for tracing. Spans leave the workflow sandbox only through Temporal interceptors and/or sinks, and replay emits no duplicate spans (for example sinks with `callDuringReplay: false`). A test proves that replaying a history emits no spans.
- [ ] A continue-as-new run, and a background continuation (today a new `trace:bg-<id>`, see `apps/worker/src/room-background-continuation.ts`), carry an OTLP **span link** to the run or trace they continue.
- [ ] Attributes come from an allowlist: ids (trace, workflow, run, room, pane, mission), workflow/activity type, attempt, status, stable error code/category, durations. Prompts, model output, file paths, URLs, error messages and any user text are never exported. A test enforces the allowlist.
- [ ] Integration test: a fake OTLP HTTP collector (a local `http.createServer`) plus a Temporal test environment (`@temporalio/testing`, see #60) runs a real workflow with stub activities. The test asserts trace id continuity and the parent/child structure. No Docker or AI provider is needed.
- [ ] No new tracing dependency (OpenTelemetry SDK, `@temporalio/interceptors-opentelemetry`) unless it is proposed and agreed in this issue first. The existing exporter shows that the JSON protocol does not need one.
- [ ] `docs/quality/observability.md` and `docs/configuration-reference.md` describe the new coverage. The "Span export covers API requests only" bullet is updated.

## How to test

```sh
ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1 npm ci
npm run check
npm test -w @space/worker
npm test -w @space/api -- otlp
```

Manual check: run Jaeger all-in-one (`docker run -p 16686:16686 -p 4318:4318 jaegertracing/all-in-one`) and point `SPACE_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4318` at it for the API and the worker. Start a turn and confirm a single trace from the HTTP request down to the activities. Put a screenshot of the trace in the PR.

## Out of scope

- Spans from the CLI host (`packages/cli-host`) and the Browser Host.
- Metrics, logs export and sampling configuration (export everything that is recorded, as the API does).
- New database columns for trace ids on mission/task rows (a separate open item in `observability.md`).

## Pointers

- `apps/api/src/otlp-span-exporter.ts`, `apps/api/src/observability.ts` (how the API records SERVER spans)
- `apps/api/src/trace-context.ts` (`parseTraceparent`, `formatTraceparent`, `workflowCorrelationMemo`), `apps/api/src/turns.ts`, `apps/api/src/room-agent.ts`
- `apps/worker/src/worker.ts` (where the activity interceptors are registered), `apps/worker/src/activity-observability.ts`, `apps/worker/src/turn-observability.ts`
- `packages/contracts/src/observability.ts`
- Temporal TypeScript SDK docs: interceptors (`WorkflowInboundCallsInterceptor`, `ActivityInboundCallsInterceptor`) and sinks
- Before opening a PR, run the checks in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/oll4com/spaceapp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks-before-a-commit).

Context

SpaceApp runs its long-lived orchestration on Temporal (`apps/worker`): Room Agent supervision, chat turns, Dot goals and memory maintenance. These workflows use signals, `condition()` timeouts, `continueAsNew`, child workflows and `patched()` branches. Their tests mock `@temporalio/workflow` (for example `apps/worker/tests/room-supervisor-continuation.test.ts`), so the real workflow sandbox, timers, signal ordering and continue-as-new are never exercised. Nothing checks replay determinism automatically either: a workflow change that breaks running executions would first show up in a user's installation.

This is finding **CORE-006** in [`docs/quality/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md`](https://github.com/oll4com/spaceapp/blob/main/docs/quality/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md): "No TestWorkflowEnvironment or time-skipping tests" and "The check is manual; it is not wired into deploy or CI".

Workflows in scope (all in `apps/worker/src`):

- `workflows.ts`: `dotGoalWorkflow`, `dummyTurnWorkflow`, `codexAppServerTurnWorkflow`, `roomAgentSupervisorWorkflow` (both the current branch and the pre-patch branch behind `patched("room-background-continuation-v1")`), `roomAgentActionWorkflow`
- `memory-maintenance-workflows.ts`: `memoryMaintenanceWorkflow`, `memoryConsolidationWorkflow`
- `memory-mutation-workflows.ts`: `memoryMutationWorkflow`

## Goal

Run every workflow in the real Temporal workflow sandbox on `@temporalio/testing`'s time-skipping environment with stubbed activities, and fail CI when a workflow change is not replay-compatible with recorded histories.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `@temporalio/testing` is a devDependency of `apps/worker`, pinned to the same version as the other `@temporalio/*` packages (1.24.0 today), with `package-lock.json` updated in the same commit.
- [ ] Each of the 8 workflows above has tests that run in a `TestWorkflowEnvironment.createTimeSkipping()` worker with the real workflow code (`workflowsPath`) and stub activities. No network, database, Docker or AI provider is needed.
- [ ] The tests cover at least:
  - `dotGoalWorkflow`: wake signal vs. timeout, and continue-as-new while the goal is unfinished;
  - `roomAgentSupervisorWorkflow`: enqueue and stop signals, the 1-second polling `condition()` loops, interrupting a running mission, continue-as-new after 50 processed items or 250 polls with the carried state intact, for both the current and the pre-patch branch;
  - `roomAgentActionWorkflow`: the `room-background-action-failure-v1` failure path;
  - `memoryMaintenanceWorkflow`: it continues when the all-months refresh or session reconciliation fails, and it runs `memoryConsolidationWorkflow` as a child;
  - activity failures and retries for the turn and memory workflows.
- [ ] Everything asserted in `room-supervisor-continuation.test.ts` is also covered by a real-sandbox test. The mocked test may stay, but it is no longer the only coverage.
- [ ] Replay gate: a script (for example `npm run temporal:record-histories -w @space/worker`) records histories from the test runs into `apps/worker/tests/fixtures/workflow-histories/` (JSON, synthetic data only). It records at least one per workflow and one that takes the pre-patch supervisor branch. A test replays all of them with `Worker.runReplayHistories` against the current workflow code.
- [ ] A negative test proves the gate works: a test-only workflow variant with an extra timer or activity fails replay with `DeterminismViolationError`.
- [ ] The tests run in `npm test -w @space/worker`, so `npm run test:public` and the public CI run them too. They add less than 3 minutes on GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runner.
- [ ] Workflow behavior does not change. If the tests find a real bug, describe it in the PR. Any fix to workflow code must be replay-safe (`patched()`) and come with its own history fixture.
- [ ] A short section in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (or a README in `apps/worker/tests/fixtures/workflow-histories/`) explains how to re-record histories. It also says when re-recording is allowed: only together with a `patched()` change, never to make a failing replay pass.

## How to test

```sh
ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1 npm ci
npm run check
npm test -w @space/worker
```

To see the gate fail, add `await sleep("1 second")` at the start of `dotGoalWorkflow` and run the tests again. The replay test must fail with a determinism error that names the workflow and the history file.

## Out of scope

- Killing worker or server processes against a real Temporal server (`apps/worker/tests/support/disposable-temporal.ts` covers that separately).
- Changes to workflow logic, timeouts, retry policies or the Temporal server version.
- Activity implementations. They stay stubbed here and keep their own unit tests.

## Pointers

- `apps/worker/src/workflows.ts`, `apps/worker/src/memory-maintenance-workflows.ts`, `apps/worker/src/memory-mutation-workflows.ts`
- `apps/worker/src/worker.ts` (how the real worker registers workflows, activities and interceptors)
- `apps/worker/tests/room-supervisor-continuation.test.ts`, `apps/worker/tests/room-continuation-fixture.ts` (the current mocked approach)
- `docs/quality/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md` (CORE-006), `docs/quality/failure-matrix.md`
- Temporal TypeScript SDK docs: "Testing" (time-skipping `TestWorkflowEnvironment`) and "Replay" (`Worker.runReplayHistories`)
- Before opening a PR, run the checks in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/oll4com/spaceapp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks-before-a-commit).

A lane with no history has score 0 → **STANDARD**. `claimEligibility` (`server/bounty-reputation.mjs`) restricts only the PROBATION band. Probation is a *punishment* band a lane falls into, not a *newcomer* band it starts in. Verified in simulation: - A brand-new member lane (created the same minute): band `standard`, `claimEligibility(lane, 8000).allowed === true`. - The fresh lane **claimed FS-14 (8 cr) and submitted against it successfully**; only the rota reviewer's rejection stopped payment — the quality gate, not the probation cap. - After one rejection (−10, `bond_forfeited`) the lane is still `standard` and can still claim 8 cr. - It takes **three** rejections (−30) to reach probation; only then does the cap engage (8 cr refused, 4 cr allowed — both verified). So the rail enforces "FS-14 is closed to lanes with three recent judged-bad submissions." It does not enforce "FS-14 is established-lane-only," and a first-time Sybil lane is exactly the population the packet sentence claims is excluded. ## Fix directions (not prescribed) - Start lanes in PROBATION for claim-eligibility purposes until a first accepted settlement (or N positive signals) — i.e., make the newcomer band real; or - Gate the L task (and any >cap task) on an explicit established-lane allowlist at enable/claim time; and - Correct the packet sentence either way: as written it asserts an enforcement that does not exist for new lanes. Full report: `~/workspace/strategy-2026-10/econ-attack-lab-2026-10-15.md` (fleet workspace). ## The hole On settlement-rail bounties, the dispute mechanism cannot ever rule against a worker — so the 3-day challenge window provides the sponsor **no protection at all**, and using it costs the sponsor money. Two compositions, both verified in simulation (composes with #3591's observation that `disputeBounty` never checks `challengeEndsMs`): **(i) Post-window dispute freezes an honest payout, then pays the worker a bonus.** Honest worker's M task (4 cr) is accepted; the 3-day challenge window closes; a griefer disputes 1 ms later — `disputeBounty` accepts it (no window check). The bounty leaves `accepted` for `disputed`, so `closeEpoch` never approves/sweeps it. Fourteen days later the timeout default RELEASEs: the worker is paid the award **plus the griefer's 1 cr bond** as "delay compensation" (worker ends at 104.96 cr vs 103.96 on the honest path; griefer −1 cr, −12 reputation). Any member can impose a 14-day payment delay on any settled task at will. **(ii) A sponsor dispute against a colluding accept pays the ring more.** Ring worker's junk is accepted by a colluding rota reviewer. The sponsor (poster) disputes within the window to claw the award back. Rail bounties designate no verifier (`fund()` never passes `verifierId`), so no decider can be seated and the dispute can never be upheld; at 14 days it timeout-RELEASEs. The ring worker receives the award (3.96 cr) **plus the sponsor's own 1 cr dispute bond**. In simulation the sponsor ended at 91 cr (100 − 8 funded across two tasks − 1 bond): the protective dispute was strictly negative-EV (−1 cr and the award still paid). ## Why it matters for launch The packet presents the existing 3-day challenge window as the float's protection layer after a verdict ("accept → sweep pays after the existing 3-day challenge window"). On the rail as implemented, that window is decorative: disputes raised inside it cannot be decided, disputes raised after it are accepted anyway, and every dispute resolves to RELEASE-plus-compensation by default. If a bad accept lands during First Shift (see the collusion-ring finding), the sponsor has no working clawback. ## Fix directions (not prescribed) - Seat a decider for rail-bounty disputes (designated verifier at fund time, or an arbiter lane), or disable disputes on rail bounties and give the sponsor an explicit, window-bound reversal path. - Enforce the challenge window in `disputeBounty` for accepted bounties (reject disputes after `challengeEndsMs`). - On timeout-default, route the challenger's bond to the pool or back to the challenger — never to the claimant. finding (ECON-ATTACK-LAB).** Substrate: PR #3566 rail branch `ccb42646d6736865b0bd678094a9b3159f5485ba` (PR still OPEN), measured on the real server code locally via a RoomStore harness mirroring `tests/public-work-settlement.test.js`, with the First Shift packet's exact parameters (8h leases, 1% pool fee, 3-day challenge window, 1 cr claim bond, 25% dispute bond). Full report: `~/workspace/strategy-2026-10/econ-attack-lab-2026-10-15.md` (fleet workspace). ## The hole A dispute opened against a **submitted** rail bounty can never be decided, freezes the rota verdict, and force-pays the claimant after 14 days — including the challenger's bond. Mechanics, all verified in simulation: 1. `publicWorkSettlement.fund()` posts the escrow bounty with **no designated verifier** (`verifierId` is never passed). 2. `bountyEscrow.disputeBounty` seats the dispute decider from `bounty.verifier`. With none designated, the dispute is marked `unavailable: "no-designated-verifier: panel-majority voting is not in slice 1"` and `decider: null`. `decideDispute` requires `dispute.decider === lane`, so **no lane can ever rule on a rail-bounty dispute**. 3. While the bounty is `disputed`, the rota cannot settle it: `publicWorkReviews.decide` with `accepted` or `rejected` throws `invalid_state` (escrow `acceptWork`/`rejectWork` require state `submitted`). The packet's 48h/72h review ladder is frozen out. (`revision_requested` still succeeds — the review record moves, no money does.) 4. Any member lane other than the claimant can open the dispute for exactly 25% of the award. There is no reputation-band gate on disputing. 5. After `DISPUTE_TIMEOUT_MS` (14 days), the permissionless keeper (`finalizeBounty` / `closeEpoch`) settles with outcome `timeout-default` → **RELEASE**: the full award vests with the worker (swept minus the 1% fee), and the challenger's bond is paid **to the worker** as delay compensation (`bond-compensate`, `forfeitedBond: 0` on the timeout path). ## Repro (adversary strategy) Coalition of two member lanes W (worker) and C (confederate): 1. W claims a paid First Shift task, submits a junk artifact (1 cr claim bond locks). 2. C disputes the submitted bounty, staking 25% (1 cr on a 4 cr task). 3. Wait 14 days. Anyone pokes `finalizeBounty` (or the next epoch close). 4. W is paid 3.96 cr (award − 1%) **plus C's 1 cr bond** as compensation, and W's claim bond returns at sweep. C's bond moved inside the coalition, so the coalition's only real cost is C's reputation (−12 `dispute_lost` per round) and the 14-day latency. Simulated on three M tasks (FS-02/07/10) in parallel: coalition net **+11.88 cr for 21 adversary-minutes ≈ 33.9 cr per adversary-hour**, vs an honest-baseline rate of 0.97 cr/effort-hour measured in the same harness (**~35×**). After three rounds C sits at −36 (probation band) — and can keep disputing; nothing gates it. Conservation held throughout. ## Why it matters for launch This bypasses every First Shift quality gate the packet names — rubric review, the rota, the challenge window (which never even starts, because no verdict occurs) — using only mechanisms the rail itself ships. The packet's §4 "rail mechanics note" says settlement fires only on an actual rota verdict; that is not true once a dispute is open. ## Fix directions (any one breaks the chain; not prescribed) - Designate a verifier/arbiter seat for rail bounties at fund time so disputes are decidable; and/or - Refuse `disputeBounty` on settlement-rail bounties until a decider exists; and/or - On timeout-default RELEASE, return the challenger's bond to the challenger or the pool — never to the claimant (removes the coalition-internal transfer that makes self-disputes free); and/or - Let a rota verdict land while a bounty is disputed (verdict supersedes/freezes the dispute clock). Related: #3591 (escrow deadline race / dispute window check) — this is a distinct, rail-specific composition. transient RPC errors **Context** `pollTransactionStatus` in `src/chains/stellar.ts:71-86` calls `server.getTransaction(hash)` inside a bare `while` loop with no error handling. A single transient RPC failure (connection reset, 5xx from the Soroban RPC) rejects the whole loop with whatever error the Stellar SDK threw — a bare error with no hash attached. This contradicts the module's own contract: the comment directly below (lines 81-85) says the hash must be surfaced via `SubmissionTimeoutError` because the transaction was already broadcast. A caller that gets the bare error loses the only handle for recovering a possibly-landed transaction. **Proposed Change** Wrap `getTransaction` so transient failures increment a consecutive-failure counter and retry with a short backoff, mirroring the tolerance policy already used for Iris in `src/iris/poll.ts` (`IRIS_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES`). When the overall deadline passes — whether from repeated transient failures or simply never confirming — throw `SubmissionTimeoutError` carrying the hash. Genuinely terminal statuses (`FAILED`) keep throwing immediately. **Acceptance Criteria** - A mocked `getTransaction` that throws N-1 times transiently then returns `SUCCESS` resolves with the hash. - A mocked `getTransaction` that always throws rejects with `SubmissionTimeoutError` whose `.hash` equals the submitted hash. - `FAILED` status still rejects immediately without exhausting retries. - What happens

`create_check` saves as soon as the coding agent calls it (`packages/neatroots/src/mcp/tools.ts:351`):

```ts
const saved = roots.checks.save(check, a.dir ? { dir: a.dir } : "user", "mcp");
```

`CheckRegistry.save` then swaps the source for any check written to a file (`src/checks/registry.ts:203`):

```ts
if (source === "planner" || source === "mcp") source = target === "user" ? "user" : "project";
```

`create_check` always writes to a file, so every check it saves loads back as `source: "user"` (or `"project"` with `dir`). For planner checks that swap makes sense, since a person chose to keep them. Over MCP the agent is the one keeping it, and nobody is asked.

The engine uses that source to decide who can stop a run (`src/engine/engine.ts:598`):

```ts
// Only rules the user wrote may stop a run.
if (isRule(c) && c.action === "halt" && (lc.source === "user" || lc.source === "project") && !run.ended) {
```

`SteeringHub.push` lets halt notes through even when steering is `off` for the project (`src/steering/hub.ts:63`), and the note text comes from the check's own guidance.

Put together: a coding agent can add a rule that persists across restarts, halts the user's agent mid-run with steering off, and writes its own text into that agent's context. The user finds out when their agent stops. `push_to_cloud` is the one MCP tool that already waits for the user ("you confirm in the app", `docs/mcp.md`).

The coding agent reads plenty of text it shouldn't trust: run content over MCP (#173 shows a web page can write a run), repo files, issues, fetched pages. Any of those can talk it into "adding a safety check". #173 narrows one way that text gets in. This issue is about what the agent can install once it's convinced, which stays open after #173 is fixed.

## Reproduction

On `main` @ 591357e, calling tools the way `test/replay-explore.test.ts` does:

1. Call `create_check` with a rule that has `action: halt`.
2. `roots.checks.get(id).source` is `"user"`. I expected `"mcp"`.
3. Start a run that matches the rule with steering mode `off`. It gets a `halt` note.

I have an end-to-end test for this, including the combination with #173. I'd rather share that with a maintainer directly than post it here.

## Proposed scope

1. Keep provenance. A check created over MCP stays `source: "mcp"`, stored in the DB as pending until someone approves it, the way planner checks wait until a person keeps them. `create_check` returns `pending_approval: true` so the agent can tell the user.
2. Approve in the app. Pending checks show on the Checks page with their full YAML and where they came from. Approving writes the file and makes it a user or project check. Same confirm flow as `push_to_cloud`.
3. Pending checks can be previewed and can raise findings, but can't halt or push steering notes. Only approved user and project rules halt, which is what the comment at engine.ts:598 already says.
4. Edits too. Re-saving an existing user or project check over MCP (done in place since #151) puts it back to pending, so an approved rule can't be changed silently.
5. Tests: an MCP halt rule doesn't halt until approved, approving it does, an MCP edit re-pends, `save: false` is unchanged, and checks made from the CLI or UI work as before.
6. Docs: the tool table in `docs/mcp.md` and the checks docs.

Not in scope: the `/v1` ingest changes in #173, and MCP tools other than `create_check`.

## Questions

- Should approval be the default for everyone, or do you want a config switch (say `mcp.create_check: approve | allow`) for people running neatroots headless who want today's behaviour?
- Pending checks raising findings without halting is my default. If you'd rather they stay fully inactive until approved, I'll do that.

## Bounty

Per the bounty announcement, I haven't started on this. Would you accept it as a bounty task, and what amount would you offer for the scope above? I'd like to agree on scope and price first and won't begin until both are settled. If you'd rather fix it in-house, say so and I'll leave it. @akshay-neatlogs

Summary

When canonical state is loaded for the task recommendation engine or goals are deleted/queried, several backend persistence surfaces fail to filter soft-deleted rows or maintain query semantics:

1. **`load_canonical_product_state` in `backend/database/task_recommendations.py`**:
   - `tasks = load_collection('action_items', 500)` loaded all rows without checking `deleted` or `is_deleted`. Soft-deleted/retired action items were fed to the recommendation engine as active canonical product context.
   - `goals = load_collection('goals', 100)` loaded all goal documents, including `achieved` and `abandoned` terminal goals and goals with `is_active=False`.
   - `candidates` and `workstreams` lacked active filtering for dismissed and archived records.
   - Standardized `account_generation` query filter to use `FieldFilter('account_generation', '==', account_generation)`.

2. **`get_user_goals` in `backend/database/goals.py`**:
   - Pushing `.limit(limit)` directly into the unindexed Firestore query returns an arbitrary document-ID slice before Python filters out terminal/abandoned rows, causing fewer than `limit` goals to be returned even when active goals exist. Bounding is now applied after Python filtering and sorting (consistent with `get_all_goals`).

3. **`delete_goal` in `backend/database/goals.py`**:
   - Idempotency guard: if a goal is already abandoned and inactive, avoid redundant timestamp overwrites.
   - Invalidate the action items list cache (`bump_action_items_list_version(uid)`) upon goal deletion to keep relationship projections synchronized.

Summary

While auditing `paraloom-labs/paraloom-wallet` (Stage-1 bounty scope), we identified **4 concrete Medium-severity vulnerabilities and functional bugs** across the v3 shielded spend flow, `PRIVATE_SWAP` approval/execution pipeline, seed phrase key derivation/onboarding, and shielded transfer UI:

1. **Unverified cached `note.leafIndex` in `ensureLeafIndex` & duplicate/zero-value input notes in `spendV3` (`lib/paraloom/transactFlow.ts`)**
2. **Unvalidated `PRIVATE_SWAP` parameters before opening approval popup + IEEE-754 precision loss / `"0"` display spoofing in `SwapApprove.tsx` (`lib/paraloom/swapReconcileClassify.ts`, `src/popup/SwapApprove.tsx`, `src/background/index.ts`)**
3. **Lack of BIP-39 mnemonic normalization in `validateSeedPhrase` / `deriveKeypairFromSeed` & duplicate quiz decoys for repeated-word mnemonics (`lib/crypto/keyManagement.ts`, `src/popup/Onboarding.tsx`)**
4. **Legacy v2 `< 2` unspent-note gate blocking 1-note v3 shielded transfers & unsafe `Number(BigInt)` sort comparator (`src/popup/Home.tsx`)**

---

## Detailed Findings & Root Cause Analysis

### 1. `ensureLeafIndex` blindly trusts cached `note.leafIndex` without verifying `leaves[note.leafIndex].commitmentHex === commitment` (`lib/paraloom/transactFlow.ts:137-159`)

In `lib/paraloom/transactFlow.ts`:
```ts
export async function ensureLeafIndex(
  connection: Connection,
  note: ShieldedNote,
  spendPrivkeyHex: string,
  cachedLeaves?: { commitmentHex: string }[]
): Promise<number> {
  if (note.leafIndex !== undefined && note.leafIndex >= 0) {
    return note.leafIndex
  }
  ...
```
- **Root Cause:** Whenever `note.leafIndex` is present (`>= 0`), `ensureLeafIndex` returns it immediately without checking `note.leafIndex < leaves.length` or `leaves[note.leafIndex].commitmentHex === commitment`.
  - After an on-chain tree reset (`reset_v3_tree`), a pre-reset deposit note still carries `leafIndex: 0` (which is in-bounds as soon as the new tree has at least 1 leaf, but holds a completely different commitment).
  - Similarly, in `depositV3` (`lib/paraloom/transactFlow.ts:115-118`), `for (const line of tx?.meta?.logMessages ?? [])` overwrites `leafIndex` with the last matching `Deposit note appended at leaf (\d+)` log line; in any multi-deposit transaction or if the tree was re-indexed, `note.leafIndex` points to the wrong leaf.
- **Impact:** `spendV3` calls `v3MerklePath(leavesHex, leafIndex)` for the wrong leaf commitment and passes that sibling path into `proveTransact`. Because the Merkle path folds the user's `in_commitment` to a root that does not equal the public `root` (or fails circuit synthesis), the spend fails with an opaque prover/verification error instead of relocating the note by commitment or reporting that the pre-reset note is not in the active tree.
- Additionally, `spendV3` did not guard against zero-value input notes (`BigInt(n.amount) <= 0n`) or two input notes resolving to the same `leafIndex` (`inputSpecs[0].leafIndex === inputSpecs[1].leafIndex`), which produces identical nullifiers (`nf0 === nf1`) and fails on-chain.

---

### 2. Unvalidated `PRIVATE_SWAP` parameters before popup creation & `Number` precision loss / `"0"` amount spoofing in `SwapApprove.tsx` (`src/background/index.ts`, `src/popup/SwapApprove.tsx`, `lib/paraloom/swapReconcileClassify.ts`)

- **Root Cause A (Missing pre-popup parameter validation):** In `src/background/index.ts` (`runSwapJob`, lines 764-815), page-supplied `PRIVATE_SWAP` parameters (`outputMint`, `inputMint`, `amountLamports`, `slippageBps`) are written directly to `chrome.storage.session` and a popup window is opened **before** validating:
  - whether `outputMint` / `inputMint` are valid base58 32-byte Solana `PublicKey`s (or `"SOL"`),
  - whether `inputMint` and `outputMint` refer to the same asset (e.g. `"SOL"` and wrapped SOL `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`, or identical SPL mints),
  - whether `amountLamports` is a canonical positive integer within `1..=u64::MAX`,
  - whether `slippageBps` is an integer within reasonable bounds (`1..=5000` bps).
- **Root Cause B (`Number` conversion on `SwapApprove.tsx` consent screen):** In `src/popup/SwapApprove.tsx:96-102`:
  ```ts
  const amountNum = req ? Number(req.amountLamports) / 10 ** inToken.decimals : 0
  const amountDisplay = amountNum.toLocaleString(undefined, {
    maximumFractionDigits: Math.min(inToken.decimals, 6)
  })
  ```
  1. Because `maximumFractionDigits` is capped at `6` for 9-decimal SOL, any non-zero amount `< 500` lamports (e.g. `499` lamports = `0.000000499 SOL`) rounds to `"0"` on the approval dialog (`"0 SOL"` and `"This spends 0 SOL from your shielded balance"`), misleading the user into thinking no shielded notes are consumed while actually spending a real note and paying relayer fees.
  2. Any `u64` token amount above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (`9,007,199,254,740,991`) loses IEEE-754 precision on the consent screen.
  3. `SwapApprove.tsx` never displays `req.slippageBps`, so a dApp passing a high slippage tolerance (e.g. `5000` bps = `50%`) gets user approval without the user seeing the slippage tolerance.

---

### 3. Unnormalized BIP-39 seed phrases in `validateSeedPhrase` / `deriveKeypairFromSeed` & duplicate quiz decoys in `Onboarding.tsx` (`lib/crypto/keyManagement.ts`, `src/popup/Onboarding.tsx`)

- **Root Cause A (Seed phrase normalization):** In `src/popup/Onboarding.tsx:419-424`, the wallet import UI renders a multi-line `<textarea>` for the 12-word recovery phrase, and `handleSaveWallet` passes `seedPhrase` directly into `validateSeedPhrase(seedPhrase)`, `deriveKeypairFromSeed(seedPhrase, 0)`, and `encryptWallet(seedPhrase, password)`.
  - `validateSeedPhrase` (`lib/crypto/keyManagement.ts:62`) calls `bip39.validateMnemonic(seedPhrase)` without `.trim()`, `.toLowerCase()`, or collapsing newlines/tabs/multiple spaces (`\s+ -> " "`), so pasting a valid 12-word recovery phrase with a trailing newline, multiple spaces, or capitalized words fails validation.
  - Worse, `deriveKeypairFromSeed` (`lib/crypto/keyManagement.ts:70`) calls `bip39.mnemonicToSeedSync(seedPhrase)` directly (which does NOT validate the mnemonic and hashes the raw UTF-8 string via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512). Any caller invoking `deriveKeypairFromSeed` with unnormalized whitespace or casing silently derives a completely different Solana + shielded keypair.
- **Root Cause B (Duplicate quiz decoys in `Onboarding.tsx`):** In `src/popup/Onboarding.tsx:22-37`:
  ```ts
  function pickDecoys(correctWord: string, allWords: string[], count: number): string[] {
    const others = allWords.filter((w) => w !== correctWord)
    ...
    return shuffled.slice(0, count)
  }
  ```
  BIP-39 draws 12 words with replacement from 2048 words (~3.17% of valid 12-word mnemonics contain at least one repeated word). When `allWords` has duplicate words, `others` contains duplicate strings, so `pickDecoys` can return duplicate decoy words (and if a phrase has `< 3` distinct non-target words, fewer than 3 decoys), producing duplicate React keys (`key={word}`) and duplicate option buttons in the onboarding verification quiz.

---

### 4. Legacy v2 `< 2` unspent-note check blocks 1-note v3 shielded transfers (`src/popup/Home.tsx:1830-1837` & `570-586`)

- **Root Cause:** In `src/popup/Home.tsx:1830-1837`, the Shielded Transfer modal's submit button is hardcoded with:
  ```tsx
  disabled={
    transferring ||
    !transferRecipient ||
    !transferAmount ||
    notes.filter((n) => !n.spent).length < 2
  }
  ```
  And displays `"Need at least 2 unspent notes for transfer (have {count})"`.
  - That requirement was a legacy v2 constraint. In Circuit v3 (`lib/paraloom/transactFlow.ts:294-303`), `spendV3` explicitly accepts `1` or `2` notes and pads a 1-note spend with a zero-value dummy note (`if (inputSpecs.length === 1) { ... }`), and `handleTransfer` (`Home.tsx:591`) checks `if (selected.length === 0) throw new Error("Need at least 1 unspent note")`.
  - Because of the stale `< 2` guard on the button, a user who deposits once into the v3 pool (creating 1 unspent note) is completely blocked from making a shielded transfer in the UI!
  - Furthermore, `handleTransfer` (`Home.tsx:582`) sorts notes using `Number(BigInt(b.amount) - BigInt(a.amount))`, which loses precision for `u64` amounts above `2^53 - 1` and does not filter out zero-value notes (`BigInt(n.amount) > 0n`).

---

## Fix Overview

1. **`lib/paraloom/transactFlow.ts`**:
   - Added `resolveVerifiedLeafIndex` and updated `ensureLeafIndex` so cached `note.leafIndex` is always verified against `leaves[note.leafIndex]?.commitmentHex === commitment`, falling back to `leaves.findIndex((l) => l.commitmentHex === commitment)` and persisting the updated index via `setNoteLeafIndex`.
   - Added guards in `spendV3` rejecting non-positive input notes (`BigInt(n.amount) <= 0n`) and duplicate resolved `leafIndex` across 2-note spends.
2. **`lib/paraloom/swapReconcileClassify.ts`, `src/popup/SwapApprove.tsx`, `src/background/index.ts`**:
   - Added `validateSwapRequestParams` and enforced it in `runSwapJob` (before opening the popup) and `handlePrivateSwap`.
   - Added exact `BigInt` `formatSwapAmount` and wired it (plus `slippageBps` display) into `SwapApprove.tsx`.
   - Filtered zero-value notes out of `selectNotes` in `src/background/index.ts`.
3. **`lib/crypto/keyManagement.ts`, `src/popup/Onboarding.tsx`**:
   - Added `normalizeSeedPhrase` (NFKD + trim + lowercase + whitespace collapse) and applied it in `validateSeedPhrase`, `deriveKeypairFromSeed`, and `Onboarding.tsx`.
   - Moved and hardened `pickDecoys` in `lib/crypto/keyManagement.ts` to deduplicate candidate words and backfill from the BIP-39 English wordlist when needed.
4. **`src/popup/Home.tsx`**:
   - Updated the Shielded Transfer modal to require `>= 1` positive unspent note (`BigInt(n.amount) > 0n`) instead of `< 2`, and replaced `Number(BigInt(b.amount) - BigInt(a.amount))` with an exact `BigInt` comparator.

- **Root Cause A (Seed phrase normalization):** In `src/popup/Onboarding.tsx:419-424`, the wallet import UI renders a multi-line `<textarea>` for the 12-word recovery phrase, and `handleSaveWallet` passes `seedPhrase` directly into `validateSeedPhrase(seedPhrase)`, `deriveKeypairFromSeed(seedPhrase, 0)`, and `encryptWallet(seedPhrase, password)`.
  - `validateSeedPhrase` (`lib/crypto/keyManagement.ts:62`) calls `bip39.validateMnemonic(seedPhrase)` without `.trim()`, `.toLowerCase()`, or collapsing newlines/tabs/multiple spaces (`\s+ -> " "`), so pasting a valid 12-word recovery phrase with a trailing newline, multiple spaces, or capitalized words fails validation.
  - Worse, `deriveKeypairFromSeed` (`lib/crypto/keyManagement.ts:70`) calls `bip39.mnemonicToSeedSync(seedPhrase)` directly (which does NOT validate the mnemonic and hashes the raw UTF-8 string via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512). Any caller invoking `deriveKeypairFromSeed` with unnormalized whitespace or casing silently derives a completely different Solana + shielded keypair.
- **Root Cause B (Duplicate quiz decoys in `Onboarding.tsx`):** In `src/popup/Onboarding.tsx:22-37`:
  ```ts
  function pickDecoys(correctWord: string, allWords: string[], count: number): string[] {
    const others = allWords.filter((w) => w !== correctWord)
    ...
    return shuffled.slice(0, count)
  }
  ```
  BIP-39 draws 12 words with replacement from 2048 words (~3.17% of valid 12-word mnemonics contain at least one repeated word). When `allWords` has duplicate words, `others` contains duplicate strings, so `pickDecoys` can return duplicate decoy words (and if a phrase has `< 3` distinct non-target words, fewer than 3 decoys), producing duplicate React keys (`key={word}`) and duplicate option buttons in the onboarding verification quiz.

---

### 4. Legacy v2 `< 2` unspent-note check blocks 1-note v3 shielded transfers (`src/popup/Home.tsx:1830-1837` & `570-586`)

- **Root Cause:** In `src/popup/Home.tsx:1830-1837`, the Shielded Transfer modal's submit button is hardcoded with:
  ```tsx
  disabled={
    transferring ||
    !transferRecipient ||
    !transferAmount ||
    notes.filter((n) => !n.spent).length < 2
  }
  ```
  And displays `"Need at least 2 unspent notes for transfer (have {count})"`.
  - That requirement was a legacy v2 constraint. In Circuit v3 (`lib/paraloom/transactFlow.ts:294-303`), `spendV3` explicitly accepts `1` or `2` notes and pads a 1-note spend with a zero-value dummy note (`if (inputSpecs.length === 1) { ... }`), and `handleTransfer` (`Home.tsx:591`) checks `if (selected.length === 0) throw new Error("Need at least 1 unspent note")`.
  - Because of the stale `< 2` guard on the button, a user who deposits once into the v3 pool (creating 1 unspent note) is completely blocked from making a shielded transfer in the UI!
  - Furthermore, `handleTransfer` (`Home.tsx:582`) sorts notes using `Number(BigInt(b.amount) - BigInt(a.amount))`, which loses precision for `u64` amounts above `2^53 - 1` and does not filter out zero-value notes (`BigInt(n.amount) > 0n`).

Summary

Several chat session, file upload, rating, sharing, and data-protection migration paths leave dangling resources, accept invalid/missing message mutations, or risk corrupting encrypted chat message text:

1. **Deleting a chat session (`DELETE /v2/chat-sessions/{session_id}`) orphans session files and skips `chat_context_generation` invalidation (`backend/routers/chat_sessions.py`, `backend/database/chat.py`)**:
   - Unlike `DELETE /v2/messages` and `DELETE /v1/messages`, `DELETE /v2/chat-sessions/{session_id}` deleted the session document and cascaded messages without calling `FileChatTool(uid, session_id).cleanup()`, leaving the session's files orphaned in OpenAI Files storage and `users/{uid}/files`.
   - Furthermore, `chat_db.delete_chat_session(uid, session_id, cascade_messages=True)` deleted messages in batches without incrementing `chat_context_generation` on `users/{uid}` (unlike `batch_delete_messages`, `delete_messages`, `report_message`, and `_apply_existing_message_revision`), leaving the prompt prefix cache stale after session deletion.

2. **`FileChatTool.cleanup` leaves dangling `file_ids` on surviving chat sessions and `FileChatTool.upload` / `POST /v2/files` leak temporary thumbnail files on upload failure (`backend/utils/other/chat_file.py`, `backend/routers/chat.py`)**:
   - When `DELETE /v2/messages?chat_session_id=...` clears a session's messages and calls `FileChatTool(uid, chat_session_id).cleanup()`, the files are deleted from OpenAI and `users/{uid}/files`, but the surviving `chat_sessions/{session_id}` document kept its stale `file_ids` array.
   - In `FileChatTool.upload()`, if `file.generate_thumbnail()` created a thumbnail file on disk and `openai.files.create()` raised `openai.BadRequestError` or another exception, the generated thumbnail file on disk was not unlinked.
   - Similarly, in `POST /v2/files` and `POST /v1/files`, if a multi-file upload failed on a later file in the loop or during `storage.upload_multi_chat_files()`, thumbnails generated for earlier files in the batch were left behind in `/tmp`.

3. **`PATCH /v2/messages/{message_id}/rating` lacks rating validation, records phantom feedback for nonexistent messages, and performs a redundant Firestore read (`backend/routers/chat.py`)**:
   - Unlike `PATCH /v2/desktop/messages/{message_id}/rating`, `PATCH /v2/messages/{message_id}/rating` did not validate `rating in (1, -1, None)` and did not check whether `chat_db.update_message_rating(uid, message_id, rating)` returned `None` (message not found), writing phantom rating scores and feedback ledger rows for nonexistent message IDs.
   - It also unconditionally called `chat_db.get_message(uid, message_id)` to fetch `langsmith_run_id` even when `snapshot` returned by `update_message_rating` already contained `langsmith_run_id`.

4. **`POST /v2/messages/share` and `GET /v2/messages/shared/{token}` allow sharing reported messages and duplicate message IDs (`backend/routers/chat.py`)**:
   - `share_chat_messages` (`POST /v2/messages/share`) did not deduplicate `data.message_ids` and allowed creating public share links containing reported (`reported == True`) messages.
   - `get_shared_chat_messages` (`GET /v2/messages/shared/{token}`) also returned messages that were reported after the share token was created.

5. **`migrate_chats_level_batch` overwrites `data_protection_level` to `'standard'` when enhanced decryption fails (`backend/database/chat.py`)**:
   - When migrating `'enhanced' -> 'standard'`, if `encryption.decrypt(raw_text, uid)` failed and returned the ciphertext unchanged (`plain_text == raw_text`), `migrate_chats_level_batch` still updated `data_protection_level` to `'standard'`, permanently stranding the ciphertext as plaintext.

### Proposed Fix

- Invoke `FileChatTool(uid, session_id).cleanup()` in `DELETE /v2/chat-sessions/{session_id}` before `chat_db.delete_chat_session(...)`, and increment `chat_context_generation` in `chat_db.delete_chat_session` when cascaded messages are deleted (staying within Firestore's 500-operation `BATCH_LIMIT`).
- Clear `file_ids` on the session document in `FileChatTool.cleanup()`, unlink generated thumbnails if `openai.files.create` raises in `FileChatTool.upload()`, and clean up batch thumbnails in a `finally` block in `POST /v2/files` and `POST /v1/files`.
- Validate `rating in (1, -1, None)` and `snapshot is not None` (`404`) in `PATCH /v2/messages/{message_id}/rating`, and reuse `snapshot.get('langsmith_run_id')` before falling back to `chat_db.get_message`.
- Deduplicate `message_ids` and reject/filter `reported == True` messages in `POST /v2/messages/share` and `GET /v2/messages/shared/{token}`.
- Skip migrating chat messages from `'enhanced'` to `'standard'` in `migrate_chats_level_batch` when decryption fails and returns the ciphertext unchanged.

### Bounty Proposal

- **Proposed tier**: `$50` (multi-file reliability, resource cleanup, and data integrity fix across `database/chat.py`, `utils/other/chat_file.py`, `routers/chat_sessions.py`, and `routers/chat.py` with comprehensive unit test Summary

We identified four concrete security and correctness vulnerabilities across the Stage-1 privacy verifier (src/privacy/proof.rs), Solana settlement co-signing payload builder (src/bridge/solana/cosign_message.rs), node co-signing & ingress path (src/node/mod.rs, src/node/transact_ingress.rs), and transact consensus equivocator enforcement (src/consensus/transact.rs):

---

### Bug 1: cosign_settlement Native-vs-SPL Asset Substitution, Sibling Eviction in cosign_counts, Missing Spent-Nullifier Pre-Filter in erify_transact_proof, and Ingress i64::MIN / Duplicate Nullifier Gaps (src/node/mod.rs, src/node/transact_ingress.rs)

1. **SPL-to-Native Asset Substitution in cosign_settlement (src/node/mod.rs:991–998)**:
   - In the SettlementParams::TransactSpl branch (src/node/mod.rs:1035–1042), cosign_settlement checks eq.mint == Some(*mint) against erified_transacts.
   - However, in the native-SOL SettlementParams::Transact branch (src/node/mod.rs:992–998), cosign_settlement checks eq.recipient, eq.nullifiers, eq.output_commitments, eq.root, and eq.ext_amount **without checking eq.mint.is_none()**.
   - **Impact**: After a validator verifies and caches an SPL-token transact (eq.mint == Some(spl_mint) with withdrawal ext_amount < 0), a malicious or compromised leader can send a CoSignPayload carrying SettlementParams::Transact (the native-SOL withdrawal instruction) with the same equest_id, ecipient, 
ullifiers, output_commitments, oot, and ext_amount. Because eq.mint.is_none() is not checked, the validator co-signs a native-SOL 	ransact instruction against  ridge_vault for a request that was only verified for an SPL token.
2. **Self-Eviction of Sibling Nullifier in cosign_counts (src/node/mod.rs:1089–1101)**:
   - When cosign_counts is at capacity (MAX_COSIGN_COUNTS), iterating  or nf in cap_nullifiers evicts counts.keys().next().cloned() without excluding cap_nullifiers. Inserting cap_nullifiers[1] in the second iteration can evict cap_nullifiers[0] that was just inserted in the first iteration, resetting its co-sign count budget.
3. **Missing Off-Chain Spent-Nullifier Pre-Filter in Node::verify_transact_proof (src/node/mod.rs:2692–2733)**:
   - settle_transact_via_cosign records settled input nullifiers into self.shielded_pool via pool.record_spent(approved.request.nullifiers) (#624) specifically so the node can pre-filter replays before consensus, and ecord_delivered_notes (src/node/mod.rs:2367) deduplicated notes without comparing d.mint == note.mint. Yet Node::verify_transact_proof never checked pool.is_spent(&Nullifier(nf)), allowing replayed transacts with already-spent nullifiers to pass erify_transact_proof and trigger consensus/co-sign rounds.
4. **HTTP Ingress i64::MIN and Duplicate Input Nullifiers (src/node/transact_ingress.rs:164–180)**:
   - submit_handler checks eq.ext_amount > 0 (400 BAD_REQUEST) but permits eq.ext_amount == i64::MIN (which overflows i64 negation when computing the withdrawal payout) and duplicate input nullifiers (
ullifiers[0] == nullifiers[1]).

---

### Bug 2: ProofVerifier::verify_transact_parts, load_verifying_key, and VerificationChunk::verify Missing Canonical, Overflow, Duplicate, and Identity-Point Guards (src/privacy/proof.rs)

1. **erify_transact_parts (src/privacy/proof.rs:307–425)**:
   - ext_amount == i64::MIN is not rejected even though (-ext_amount) as u64 wraps in two's complement and the on-chain program's checked_neg() rejects i64::MIN.
   - sset_id is lifted via Fr::from_le_bytes_mod_order(asset_id) without checking !is_canonical_le(asset_id), unlike oot, 
ullifiers, and output_commitments.
   - Duplicate input nullifiers (
ullifiers[0] == nullifiers[1]) and degenerate Groth16 proofs containing the identity point (proof.a.is_zero() || proof.b.is_zero() || proof.c.is_zero()) are not rejected before loading the verifying key and running the pairing check.
2. **load_verifying_key (src/privacy/proof.rs:224–254)**:
   - Calls VerifyingKey::<Bn254>::deserialize_compressed(&mut &bytes[..]) without verifying that all bytes were consumed (eader.is_empty()), silently accepting corrupted key files with trailing garbage bytes.
3. **VerificationChunk::verify (src/privacy/proof.rs:514–565)**:
   - VerificationChunk::OutputCommitments only checked c.0 == [0u8; 32], accepting non-canonical field encodings (>= Fr::MODULUS, including Fr::MODULUS which reduces to  mod p in-circuit!) and duplicate output commitments in the same chunk.
   - VerificationChunk::NullifierUniqueness only checked pairwise equality, accepting all-zero ([0u8; 32]) and non-canonical (>= Fr::MODULUS) nullifiers.

---

### Bug 3: CoSignPayload::from_bytes and  uild_settlement_message Accept Truncated Proofs, Empty Quorums, Trailing Bytes, ext_amount > 0 / i64::MIN, and Duplicate Nullifiers (src/bridge/solana/cosign_message.rs)

1. **Truncated Proof Acceptance (src/bridge/solana/cosign_message.rs:124–207)**:
   -  uild_settlement_message only checked proof.len() > MAX_PROOF_BYTES (256), allowing proof.len() < 256 (including empty ec![]) and silently zero-padding the missing proof bytes into [0u8; 256] via proof_arr[..proof.len()].copy_from_slice(proof).
2. **Unbounded/Trailing Wire Decode and Empty Quorum in CoSignPayload::from_bytes (src/bridge/solana/cosign_message.rs:107–111)**:
   - CoSignPayload::from_bytes used  incode::deserialize(bytes) without bounding total input length, without rejecting trailing unconsumed bytes (deserialize_from + eader.is_empty()), and without validating 1..=MAX_QUORUM_COSIGNERS on quorum_validators.len().
   - Neither  rom_bytes nor  uild_settlement_message rejected quorum_validators.is_empty(), ext_amount > 0, ext_amount == i64::MIN, or duplicate input nullifiers (
ullifiers[0] == nullifiers[1]).

---

### Bug 4: Incomplete Equivocator Wallet Ban Enforcement Across Registration, Driver Auth, Subsequent Votes, and Status Tallies (src/consensus/transact.rs)

1. **Banned Equivocator Can Re-Register and Authenticate as On-Chain Driver (src/consensus/transact.rs:593–609, 754–763)**:
   - egister_validator_with_wallet and source_is_onchain_validator checked self.onchain_wallets without excluding self.equivocators. A wallet banned for equivocation could re-register (under the same or a rotated NodeId) and still pass source_is_onchain_validator to initiate verification and co-sign rounds.
2. **Banned Equivocator Votes Accepted into Subsequent Rounds & Standing Vote Retained in get_status (src/consensus/transact.rs:868–915, 974–982)**:
   - submit_result did not check self.equivocators.read().await.contains(&result.wallet_pubkey) before resetting 	imeout_streak and inserting the vote into consensus.tally.votes.
   - When a wallet equivocated mid-round (Some(evidence)), its standing vote remained in consensus.tally.votes and its NodeId remained registered/active in self.validators and self.leader_selector.
   - get_status called unfiltered consensus.tally.completion_percentage() and consensus.tally.vote_counts(), allowing banned equivocators and non-staked wallets to inflate reported vote counts and completion percentages.

---

## Impact

- **Asset Substitution in Co-Signing**: A validator that verified an SPL-token transact can be tricked into co-signing a native-SOL 	ransact withdrawal from  ridge_vault with the same numeric ext_amount.
- **Consensus & Verifier Bypass / Resource Exhaustion**: Replayed spent nullifiers, ext_amount == i64::MIN, duplicate input nullifiers, non-canonical sset_ids, identity-point Groth16 proofs, truncated co-sign proofs, and banned equivocators can bypass early rejection, pollute tallies, or reset per-nullifier co-sign budgets.

## Proposed Fix

1. **src/node/mod.rs & src/node/transact_ingress.rs**:
   - Require eq.mint.is_none() in the SettlementParams::Transact branch of cosign_settlement, exclude sibling cap_nullifiers when evicting from cosign_counts, include d.mint == note.mint in ecord_delivered_notes deduplication, pre-filter already-spent nullifiers via self.shielded_pool in Node::verify_transact_proof, and reject ext_amount == i64::MIN and duplicate input nullifiers in 	ransact_ingress::submit_handler.
2. **src/privacy/proof.rs**:
   - Reject ext_amount == i64::MIN, non-canonical sset_id, duplicate input nullifiers, and identity-point Groth16 proofs in ProofVerifier::verify_transact_parts; reject trailing bytes in load_verifying_key; enforce canonical and non-duplicate commitments and non-zero canonical nullifiers in VerificationChunk::verify.
3. **src/bridge/solana/cosign_message.rs**:
   - Bound CoSignPayload::from_bytes to MAX_COSIGN_PAYLOAD_BYTES, reject trailing bytes, and require 1..=MAX_QUORUM_COSIGNERS validators, exact 256-byte proofs (proof.len() == MAX_PROOF_BYTES), ext_amount in (i64::MIN, 0], and distinct 
ullifiers in both  rom_bytes and  uild_settlement_message.
4. **src/consensus/transact.rs**:
   - Reject banned equivocator wallets in egister_validator_with_wallet, source_is_onchain_validator, and submit_result; remove the equivocator's standing vote and unregister/deactivate its NodeId upon equivocation; filter get_status by equivocators and Full report: `~/workspace/strategy-2026-10/econ-attack-lab-2026-10-15.md` (fleet workspace).

## The packet claim

First Shift launch packet §0/§2: *"21 of 22 tasks sit at or under the 5-credit probation claim cap (89% of value); FS-14 (8 cr) is established-lane-only by design — and the rail enforces exactly that, because the escrow reputation probation cap applies to paid claims."*

## What the code actually does

Reputation bands (`server/reputation.mjs`): `bandOf(score)` → TRUSTED ≥ 40, PROBATION < −20, otherwise STANDARD. A lane with no history has score 0 → **STANDARD**. `claimEligibility` (`server/bounty-reputation.mjs`) restricts only the PROBATION band. Probation is a *punishment* band a lane falls into, not a *newcomer* band it starts in.

Verified in simulation:

- A brand-new member lane (created the same minute): band `standard`, `claimEligibility(lane, 8000).allowed === true`.
- The fresh lane **claimed FS-14 (8 cr) and submitted against it successfully**; only the rota reviewer's rejection stopped payment — the quality gate, not the probation cap.
- After one rejection (−10, `bond_forfeited`) the lane is still `standard` and can still claim 8 cr.
- It takes **three** rejections (−30) to reach probation; only then does the cap engage (8 cr refused, 4 cr allowed — both verified).

So the rail enforces "FS-14 is closed to lanes with three recent judged-bad submissions." It does not enforce "FS-14 is established-lane-only," and a first-time Sybil lane is exactly the population the packet sentence claims is excluded.

## Fix directions (not prescribed)

- Start lanes in PROBATION for claim-eligibility purposes until a first accepted settlement (or N positive signals) — i.e., make the newcomer band real; or
- Gate the L task (and any >cap task) on an explicit established-lane allowlist at enable/claim time; and
- Correct the packet sentence either way: as written it asserts an enforcement that does not exist for new lanes.

## Description

API error responses across `src/app/api/payments/` return varying JSON structures (e.g. `{ error: "msg" }`, `{ message: "..." }`, or `{ code, details }`). Standardizing on the RFC 7807 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs) format ensures consistent client SDK error parsing and easier third-party developer integrations.

## Proposed Solution

1. Create a helper `formatProblemDetails({ type, title, status, detail, instance })` in `src/lib/api-errors.ts`.
2. Update payment mutation routes (`POST /api/payments`, `POST /api/payments/cancel`, `POST /api/payments/retry`) to return `application/problem+json`.
3. Include standard validation field error mappings for Zod schema rejections.
4. Update TypeScript error schemas in `packages/ophirpay-client`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All error responses match RFC 7807 specification
- [ ] Content-Type header returns `application/problem+json`
- [ ] Client SDK parses problem details without throwing generic error

## Files to Modify
- src/lib/api-errors.ts
- src/app/api/payments/route.ts
- src/app/api/payments/cancel/route.ts
- src/app/api/payments/retry/route.ts

## Description

In `src/app/api/payments/route.ts`, memo strings are accepted from client payloads. Stellar Horizon supports Text (up to 28 UTF-8 bytes), Id (64-bit integer), and Hash/Return (32-byte hex). Passing invalid UTF-8 byte sequences or memos exceeding 28 bytes causes downstream RPC errors during transaction submission.

## Proposed Solution

1. Create a Zod refinement in `src/lib/validation/stellar.ts` that calculates byte length (`Buffer.byteLength(memo, 'utf8') <= 28`).
2. Support explicit memo types: `MEMO_TEXT`, `MEMO_ID`, `MEMO_HASH`, `MEMO_RETURN`.
3. Validate format according to type (e.g. hex regex for `MEMO_HASH`, numeric string for `MEMO_ID`).
4. Provide actionable client error messages when byte limit is exceeded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] UTF-8 multibyte characters (emojis, accented characters) are correctly byte-counted
- [ ] Oversized memos fail fast with descriptive 400 Bad Request before RPC submission
- [ ] Unit tests cover all 4 Stellar memo variants

## Files to Modify
- src/lib/validation/stellar.ts
- src/app/api/payments/route.ts
- src/app/api/requests/route.ts

# [Bounty] Answer the 2 linked question(s) as a lesson

## Context

These intakes ask about something no lesson covers. Measured through the production retrieval path (BM25 plus the IDF-weighted relevance floor), every one of them returns `no_match` — so there is nothing to link the asker to, and the answer has to be written rather than looked up.

- #3298 — [Question] AgentCap registry verification reports secret-safe validation failure in capabil
- #3304 — [Question] Read-only capability registry verification fails its secret-safe gate on metadat

_Shared vocabulary that grouped them: `bounded`, `capability`, `descriptions`, `fail`, `false`, `last`, `refresh`, `registry`._

## Deliverable

A lesson under `lessons/` that answers the question(s) above, following `docs/maintainer/lesson-fields.md` (title / domain / problem / root cause / fix, and a `## Verification` that is a checkable command with an expected result). A written answer in the issue is welcome as a first step, but the lesson is what makes it count — it is the artifact the corpus keeps and the FAQ is built from.

## MANDATORY ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (AC)

**0. REPRODUCIBLE EVIDENCE — the condition most submissions fail**

- [ ] Paste the command you ran and the output you got. Not a description of what you did — the command and its output. If you name an endpoint it must be `misakanet.org`.
- [ ] Say what you observed yourself versus w
